data: © Soviet Academy of Sciences (historical). Sample mass: 170 g of regolith returned to Earth 1976-08-22.

The last Soviet lunar mission — and the last uncrewed Moon landing until China's Chang'e 3 in 2013: a gap of 37 years. Returned 170 g of samples including minerals containing water, foreshadowing the later discovery of lunar water ice.
Demonstrated robotic sample return — the architecture Mars Sample Return is now attempting at interplanetary scale.

Luna 24 landed in Mare Crisium on August 18, 1976 — the last Soviet (and last robotic) lunar sample-return mission of the 20th century, and the last lunar lander of any kind until China's Chang'e 3 in 2013. Drilled 2 m into the regolith, returned 170.1 g of samples to Earth, including evidence of lunar water ice (re-confirmed decades later by SOFIA + LCROSS). The Soviet lunar program ended here.
Soviet E-8-5M lander — improved sample-return rig
Luna 24 spacecraft on display at a Soviet space museum — descent stage + ascent vehicle + return capsule.
The drill mechanism — went 2 m deep, three times farther than Luna 16's 35 cm. Returned the deepest samples ever brought from another world.
Mare Crisium landing site — Luna 24 touched down ~2 km from Luna 23's failed 1974 landing in the same region.
Return capsule in Siberia, August 22 1976 — last Soviet sample-return from beyond Earth orbit until VKS programs of the 2020s.
Re-analysis of Luna 24 samples in 1978 reported 0.1% water content — initially dismissed, confirmed by LCROSS impact + SOFIA in 2020.
